record.paper_title: An Overview of Compact Star Populations and Some of Its Open Problems
record.original_question: Do neutron-star magnetic fields genuinely decay over astrophysical timescales, and if so do they fade almost completely within about 10^6 years or instead decay only partially to a persistent 'bottom field' that remains substantial even in very old systems such as black widows?

evidence.quote: This question is one of the oldest, and has been answered differently over the years. The idea that there must be a decay of the field within ∼106 yr is quite popular
Magnetic fields may decay partially to a “bottom field”, but not completely

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A neutron star is a compact stellar remnant endowed with a magnetic field whose surface strength B can be inferred from pulsar timing (via the spin period P and its derivative). Observations of neutron star populations across a wide range of ages (from young pulsars at ages ~10^3–10^6 yr to recycled millisecond pulsars and "black widow" systems with characteristic ages ≳10^9 yr) raise the following question about the long-term evolution of B(t):

Determine whether the magnetic field of an isolated or binary neutron star genuinely decays as a function of age on astrophysical timescales, and if so characterize the asymptotic behavior. Specifically, decide between the following competing scenarios and identify the physical mechanism responsible:

(a) B(t) decays almost completely on a timescale of order 10^6 years, so that very old neutron stars retain only negligible magnetic fields;

(b) B(t) decays only partially toward a finite, non-zero "bottom field" B_min > 0 that persists even in systems with evolution times ≳10^9 yr, as suggested by inferred field strengths of black-widow pulsars and other very old recycled systems.

Provide a quantitative model B(t) (including dependence on accretion history, crustal impurity, and thermal evolution) that is consistent with the observed distribution of magnetic field strengths in the full neutron-star population, and either establish the existence and value of B_min or rule it out.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether neutron-star magnetic fields decay completely or only partially to a non-zero "bottom field" remains an active open problem. Studies of black-widow pulsars indicate the field does not fall below a minimum value despite very long evolution times, but the underlying mechanism (linked to anomalies in neutron-star cooling models and the role of crustal impurity) is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic field decay in black widow pulsars
status_evidence.snippet: The magnetic field does not fall below a minimum value ('bottom field') in spite of the long evolution time of the black widow systems.
status_evidence.claim: Observational evidence supports the existence of a non-zero bottom field, but the mechanism remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic field decay in black widow pulsars - ADS
status_evidence.snippet: The existence of a bottom field is likely related to the fact that the surface temperature of the pulsar does not decay as predicted by current cooling models.
status_evidence.claim: The physical origin of the bottom field is tied to unresolved issues in neutron-star cooling theory.
